quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, move to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in heavy traffic, slow down and move right as soon as you can.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Is loose.
Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden beneath the seat.
Keeps the seat belt buzzer or light from operating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable with room for your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?

options.text: Under no circumstances.
When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren.

questions.question: When can you carefully continue through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: There is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.
There are pedestrians crossing.
You are turning right.
You are already within the intersection when the light changes to yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already within the intersection when the light changes to yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you can continue through carefully.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Under no conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to make a U-turn where permitted.

questions.question: What should you do if your right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Immediately pull all the way off of the road and get back on when it is safe.
Accelerate and steer back on the road quickly.
Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the road, stay calm. Release the accelerator and slow down. Keep both hands on the wheel and ease back onto the road with a small turn. Check for traffic before returning to the pavement.

questions.question: What does an octagonal sign always mean?

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red eight-sided sign.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When a funeral procession is present, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Another driver
A pedestrian
The funeral procession
A bicyclist

questions.correctAnswerText: The funeral procession
questions.explanation: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield to funeral processions. Once the lead vehicle enters an intersection, all vehicles in the procession may follow through, regardless of traffic signals.

questions.question: What does it mean when a driver extends their left arm and hand upward?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they are signaling a right turn. Adjust your driving if you are following this vehicle.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start from the left lane when turning left from multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and request an ambulance if needed. Help stop any severe bleeding with direct pressure. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Wait for emergency responders.

questions.question: When you turn left onto a one-way street, which lane should you end up in?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to your previous lane.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to the direction you came from.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light mean?

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and prepare to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and get ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not pass.
Do not enter.
No turn on red.
Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is ahead. The road will split into two one-way roads with a median between them. Stay to the right.

questions.question: What should you do when you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Retaliate by tailgating them.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between your vehicle and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: You are backing out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Get out and check behind your vehicle before backing up. Look through your back window and mirrors. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially near children.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: That is parked on the shoulder of the road with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
If you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights stopped to pick up or drop off children. On a two-lane road, traffic from both directions must stop while the red lights flash or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has a sharp right turn followed by a sharp left turn.

questions.question: What must a driver do when dealing with pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian is aware of their vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.
Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.
Slow down and sound their horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.
questions.explanation: Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are just suggestions.
Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign:

options.text: Warns of existing or possible hazards.
Alerts drivers to school zones.
Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
Alerts drivers to upcoming food and gas locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns of existing or possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards on the road. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are approaching.
Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Proceed carefully through the intersection without always stopping.
Stop only for traffic on an intersecting road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a full stop. Yield to vehicles and pedestrians in or near the intersection. Go again when it is safe.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means that, unless directed by a police officer, you may stop only:

options.text: Long enough to unload packages.
To avoid conflict with other traffic.
To let passengers out.
For less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid conflict with other traffic.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, follow a police officer's directions, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or air horns with red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so move only when the way is clear.

questions.question: You are angry after an incident at work. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
questions.explanation: Do not drive when you are upset or angry. Take time to calm down first. Driving while emotional is dangerous to yourself and others.

questions.question: When driving in fog:

options.text: Use your parking lights.
Use your low beams.
Use your high beams.
It makes no difference which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. You should:

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, yield the right-of-way, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: You may use your horn when you:

options.text: Have to stop quickly.
Are passing another car.
Have lost control of your car.
Are passing a bicycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: You notice a defect that may affect safe operation of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you can afford it.
Drive the vehicle at slower speeds.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that may affect safe operation of your vehicle as soon as possible. Repair it before driving.

questions.question: When a traffic signal turns green, you should:

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up as fast as you can.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. But first, make sure no pedestrians or other traffic are still in the intersection. Let them clear before you move.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and check if it is coming toward you.
Slow down but do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and check if it is coming toward you.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, pull safely to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not headed toward you.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, you should:

options.text: Do nothing special.
Honk your horn.
Pass as close to the animal as possible.
Be very careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very careful.
questions.explanation: Always be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you do not scare it or cause it to move into your path.

questions.question: When is it safe to use cruise control?

options.text: In heavy traffic.
On country roads with light traffic.
In heavy rain or snow.
When pulling a heavy trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: On country roads with light traffic.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic, near exits and entrances, or on wet or icy roads. Constantly adjusting cruise control is distracting and increases crash risk. Do not use it when towing heavy loads.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before you change lanes or pass. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as few times as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: A good rule for passing is:

options.text: Always pass on the right.
Drive with traffic and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic to see better.
Always flash lights and honk to warn drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass, there is more risk of a crash. If you drive faster than other traffic, you will need to keep passing. Drive with the flow of traffic within the speed limit and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area.
The fastest or slowest speed you can legally drive.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you can legally drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the legal maximum or minimum speed allowed. These limits are for ideal conditions. You must drive slower when road or weather conditions are poor.

questions.question: To avoid headlight glare at night, look:

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
At the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look toward the right edge of the road. Do not stare at the headlights. The glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: Before turning left, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking your mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming cars and people.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal 3 to 5 seconds before you turn left. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. Move into the left lane before the intersection. Wait until it is safe and the path is clear before you turn.

questions.question: You cannot cross a single broken white or yellow line if:

options.text: It would get in the way of other traffic.
You are turning left into a driveway.
The car ahead of you has broken down.
You are passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: It would get in the way of other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely and without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
A divided highway is starting. Slow down to 35 mph.
Merge ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
A winding road is ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road curves to the right. Slow down to the safe speed shown on the sign (35 mph in this case).

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep driving at your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians cross first.
Drive faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: You can turn right on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When you turn, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What can help you avoid rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid stopping suddenly.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal before using the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop suddenly and the driver behind you may hit you. Instead, release the gas pedal first to let your car slow down, then press the brake pedal gently. This lights up your brake lights and gives the driver behind you time to react.

questions.question: What road space are motorcycles allowed to use?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as cars and trucks.
Half the width of a normal lane.
The sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the entire lane width, just like any other vehicle.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop right away and block the emergency vehicle.
Pull to the side and give it a clear path.
Signal when it is safe for it to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side and give it a clear path.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the side of the road if you can do so safely. This gives the emergency vehicle a clear path to travel.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very rare.
Very dangerous.
Not a concern.
As safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Very dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Pay full attention to the road to prevent crashes.

questions.question: At a light rail crossing, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Follow all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and cyclists.
Do all of these things.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of these things.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing tracks. Follow all signs and traffic signals. Remember that trains share the road with cars and bicycles.

questions.question: When passing a car on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Move back to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the other car.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left soon.
Move back to the right lane right away.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move back to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the other car.
questions.explanation: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, move back to the right lane when you have enough space between your car and the car you passed.

questions.question: When driving in the rain, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your high beam headlights.
Use your parking lights.
Do not use any lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In rain, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After completing the turn, your car should be in:

options.text: The right lane.
The center of the street.
The left lane.
The lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, finish the turn in the lane closest to where you came from.
